title: Evaluate a sealed expression tree

blocks.text: Records under a sealed interface, taken apart by record patterns, make an exhaustive switch: when every permitted record has a case, no `default` is needed, and the compiler refuses the switch if a new kind of expression is added and not handled. A `default` arm would hide that missing case instead.

`Calc` holds `sealed interface Expr permits Num, Add, Sub, Mul, Neg` and its five records: `Num(int value)`, `Add(Expr left, Expr right)`, `Sub(Expr left, Expr right)`, `Mul(Expr left, Expr right)` and `Neg(Expr operand)`.
Write `eval(Expr expr)` in `Calc` as one switch over record patterns, with no `default`:

items: `eval(new Add(new Num(2), new Mul(new Num(3), new Num(4))))` is `14`;
`eval(new Sub(new Num(10), new Num(4)))` is `6`: left minus right;

cases.says: Sub(10, 4) is 6: the right side is taken from the left.
Neg(5) is -5: a default arm must not stand in for a missing case.

concepts: Over a sealed interface of records, a switch of record patterns is exhaustive with no default, and a default would hide a missing case.
